subject: math

objective.text: Solve two-step word problems about dollars or cents, with totals within 100 dollars or 1 dollar.

explanations.title: Draw a model first
explanations.text: Before you solve, think about the model. A tape diagram or a number bond shows the parts and the whole. Think about the operation and a strategy too.

explanations.title: Find the missing coin
explanations.text: Find the value of the coins you know. Count up or subtract to reach the new total. The difference is the value of the missing coin.

explanations.title: Two steps
explanations.text: Some problems have two parts. Find one amount first. Then use it to find the answer. Use two tape diagrams of the same size, and make one longer for the extra.

explanations.title: Find the start
explanations.text: When money was spent and some is left, the cost and the money left are two parts. Add them to find what you had at the start.

explanations.title: Skip-count the money
explanations.text: Skip-count by tens, then fives, then ones. For bills, skip-count by fives and ones. This helps you find one part quickly.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Parts 1 and 3; Student Debrief

explanations.title: 100 cents in nickels
explanations.text: 100 cents is the same as 20 nickels. You can also find the value of the coins and take it from 100.

examples.title: Gary's missing coin
examples.text: Gary has 2 dimes, 5 nickels and 13 pennies. That is 58 cents. A coin from his brother makes 68 cents. 68 minus 58 equals 10. The coin is a dime.

examples.title: Hailey's snack
examples.text: The pretzel stick costs a dime and a nickel, or 15 cents. The juice box costs 18 cents more, so it costs 33 cents. 15 plus 33 equals 48. Hailey spent 48 cents.

examples.title: Wendell's game
examples.text: Wendell has 2 five-dollar bills and 4 one-dollar bills left. That is 14 dollars. The game cost 16 dollars. 16 plus 14 equals 30. He had 30 dollars at the start.

questions.text: In a decomposition tree, 100 is the whole. One part is 60. What is the other part?
In a decomposition tree, 100 is the whole. One part is 35. What is the other part?

Dante had some money in a jar. He puts 8 nickels into the jar. Now he has 100 cents. How much money was in the jar at first, in cents?
Gary has 2 dimes, 5 nickels and 13 pennies. How many cents is that?
Gary's brother gives him one more coin. Now Gary has 68 cents. What coin did his brother give him?
Hailey bought a pretzel stick for a dime and a nickel. How many cents did it cost?
Hailey's juice box cost 18 cents more than the pretzel stick. How much did the juice box cost, in cents?
How much did Hailey spend on the pretzel stick and the juice box, in cents?
Wendell has 2 five-dollar bills and 4 one-dollar bills left after buying a game. How many dollars is that?
Wendell bought a game for 16 dollars. He has 14 dollars left. How many dollars did he have before he bought the game?
Josephine has 3 nickels, 4 dimes and 12 pennies. Her mother gives her 1 coin. Now Josephine has 92 cents. What coin did her mother give her?
Christopher has 3 ten-dollar bills, 3 five-dollar bills and 12 one-dollar bills. Jenny has 19 dollars more than Christopher. How many dollars does Jenny have?
Isaiah started with 2 twenty-dollar bills, 4 ten-dollar bills, 1 five-dollar bill and 7 one-dollar bills. He spent 73 dollars on clothes. How many dollars does he have left?
Jackie bought a sweater for 42 dollars. She had 3 five-dollar bills and 6 one-dollar bills left over. How many dollars did she have before she bought the sweater?
Mary found 98 cents in her piggy bank. She counted 1 quarter, 8 pennies, 3 dimes and some nickels. How many nickels did she count?
Akio found 18 cents in one pocket. He found 6 more coins in his other pocket. Altogether he has 73 cents. How many cents are the 6 coins worth?
Akio's 6 coins in his other pocket are worth 55 cents. What could the 6 coins be?
Gary went to the store with 4 ten-dollar bills, 3 five-dollar bills and 7 one-dollar bills. He bought a sweater for 26 dollars. How many dollars does he have left?
Gary has 36 dollars left after he bought a sweater. What bills could he have left the store with?
Kelly bought a pencil sharpener for 47 cents and a pencil for 35 cents. What was her change from 1 dollar, in cents?
Hae Jung bought a pretzel for 3 dimes and a nickel. She also bought a juice box. She spent 92 cents. How much was the juice box, in cents?
Monique saved 2 ten-dollar bills, 4 five-dollar bills and 15 one-dollar bills. Harry saved 16 dollars more than Monique. How many dollars did Harry save?
Ryan went shopping with 3 twenty-dollar bills, 3 ten-dollar bills, 1 five-dollar bill and 9 one-dollar bills. He spent 59 dollars on a video game. How many dollars does he have left?
Heather had 3 ten-dollar bills and 4 five-dollar bills left after buying sneakers for 29 dollars. How many dollars did she have before she bought the sneakers?
Nolan has 1 quarter, 1 nickel and 21 pennies. His brother gave him 2 coins. Now he has 86 cents. What 2 coins did his brother give him?
Before you solve a word problem, what should you think about?
How can skip-counting help you solve one part of a money problem quickly?
How did a tape diagram or number bond help you solve a problem today?

hints.text: Find the value of the coins you know first.
Compare the new total to the amount before. The difference is the missing part.
More than means add on. Find the first cost, then add the extra.
The cost and the money left are the parts. Add them to find the start.
Find the value of the nickels. The number of coins is not the same as their value.
Count the bills by tens, then fives, then ones.

misconceptions.label: Subtracts the number of coins
misconceptions.description: The child subtracts the number of coins from 100 instead of finding the value of the coins.
misconceptions.response_text: 8 is how many coins. It is not their value. Find the value of 8 nickels first. Then use 100.
